phase: Reference Mode Recovery — Sectoral Financial Positions / Phase D source-discrepancy localization
scientific_interpretation: The Phase C stock discrepancy is not primarily an external-sector orientation problem. In every Phase C failing stock quarter, the dominant component is the difference between the sum of published resident-sector aggregates and the directly published total-economy S1 aggregate.
The direct total-economy versus rest-of-world relation is much tighter, with a maximum absolute stock discrepancy of approximately 0.01 million RON.
The decomposition is exact up to computational precision, so the localization is algebraic rather than interpretive.
Because the required reference mode is sectoral, direct S1 totals cannot replace the H/C/F/G/BNR histories without changing the scientific target after observing the result.
No residual may be allocated to a sector. The observed public-data inconsistency is retained as a source-boundary limitation.
